articles.title: Looking for lateral movement with a neural network trained on synthetic data
articles.excerpt: Can you train a cyberattack detector without ever showing it a real cyberattack? It sounds like a contradiction. If you want a neural network to detect lateral movement, you would expect to show it la…
articles.body: Can you train a cyberattack detector without ever showing it a real cyberattack? It sounds like a contradiction. If you want a neural network to detect lateral movement, you would expect to show it lateral movement. I did the opposite: I generated an entire corporate network with its login history, staged an attack inside that artificial world, and trained networks on it. Not a single real row in the training data. The whole world is a 135-line config; each network has four thousand parameters and trains in seconds on a laptop, and the best result came from six of them, trained on six different invented worlds. Then I pointed them at real data: the authentication logs of Los Alamos National Laboratory, 1.65 billion events, with red-team exercises labelled in them. And it worked.

articles.body: Sherlock Pay (repo name: UPI Fraud Ring Detective) is our Graph Hacks project: an AI agent that takes **one * flagged UPI payment, walks a FalkorDB graph, and comes back with the whole mule ring, a decision for every account, and the exact Cypher behind each step.* A video call one afternoon Anil Mehta's phone rings. A man in a police uniform on a video call says Anil's Aadhaar was used to send drugs abroad. He is under "digital arrest". He must not hang up, must not tell his family, and must move ₹1,85,000 to a "verification account" to prove his innocence. Anil pays. One UPI payment, a few taps. Anil isn't real. He lives in the synthetic dataset we built for this hackathon.

Establish the state contract For a booking assistant, distinguish extracted suggestions from user-confirmed values. Specify which state a summary or dispatch worker must read and which events can invalidate confirmation. A prompt asking the model to respect edits may help guide generation. The application still needs to enforce its rules when saving data or preparing an action. Define how conflicts are resolved before writing assertions.

On October 17, 2026, the GitHub repository had about 94,300 stars, and the stirlingtools/stirling-pdf image had about 16.3 million pulls on Docker Hub, plus 22.5 million under the older frooodle/s-pdf name, which still gets new releases. This guide runs Stirling-PDF 3.2.0 with Docker Compose and fixes the parts the quick start leaves to you. articles.title: A perfect ATS score means nothing about being picked
articles.excerpt: Every quarter, a fresh crop of utilities sells the promise of a ninety-five percent ATS score. Candidates buy keyword injection tools, rename sections to match proprietary parsers, and test their sour…
articles.body: Every quarter, a fresh crop of utilities sells the promise of a ninety-five percent ATS score. Candidates buy keyword injection tools, rename sections to match proprietary parsers, and test their source files against ten different compliance checkers until the dials turn green. Then they wait. The queue does not move. The interview rate stays flat. This happens because people confuse clearing a mechanical floor with winning an argument. An applicant tracking system is a filter, not an arbiter. It answers a binary question about whether a document can be parsed into structured database fields without dropping dates or job titles. Passing that check means you are legible to the machine. It does nothing to prove that you should be called for a conversation.

articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.body: HBO and HBO Max's " Lanterns " served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were. While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling. After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
